name: Caesium
blurb: 133Cs is 100% abundant, spin 7/2, and carries one of the smallest quadrupole moments of any nucleus with I > 1/2 (Q = -0.343 fm2), so its lines stay narrow even in disordered solids and it behaves almost like a spin-1/2 nucleus. Caesium vapour cells are the sensing element of SERF and Mx atomic magnetometers used for ultra-low-field MRI and zero-field NMR detection.
mrNotes: Xi(133Cs) = 13.116142 %, reference 0.1 M CsNO3 in D2O; receptivity is 283 times 13C, so single scans suffice at millimolar concentration.
Cs+ is a slow K+ congener; 133Cs MRS has tracked cation transport in perfused hearts and in whole rodents, with T1 of order seconds.
Caesium also substitutes for rubidium as the alkali in spin-exchange optical pumping of 129Xe, pumped on the 894 nm D1 line instead of 795 nm.
137Cs (30.08 y) is the gamma source in blood irradiators and legacy brachytherapy tubes, not an imaging tracer.

isotopes.notes: Q of only -0.343 fm2 keeps second-order quadrupolar broadening small; solid CsCl sits at +223 ppm while aqueous Cs+ salts fall within about 10 ppm of the reference. Caesium metal has a Knight shift far outside this window.
Fission product and sealed gamma source (662 keV). Receptivity computes to zero because natural abundance is zero; the nucleus itself is NMR-active in enriched material.

name: Barium
blurb: Both barium NMR isotopes are low-gamma quadrupolar nuclei whose lines are broad even in cubic sites, so barium matters to MR through its materials rather than its spectrum. Barium titanate slurries are the high-permittivity dielectric pads used to reshape B1+ at 7 T, and barium sulfate suspensions serve as a negative oral bowel marker in MR enterography.
mrNotes: Xi(137Ba) = 11.112928 % and Xi(135Ba) = 9.934457 %, both referenced to 0.5 M BaCl2 in D2O.
137Ba has about 2.4 times the receptivity of 135Ba but a 1.5 times larger Q; solid-state work needs 18.8 T plus QCPMG or WURST-echo acquisition.
BaTiO3 suspensions with relative permittivity of a few hundred are placed against the body at 7 T to raise local transmit efficiency and cut SAR.
133Ba (10.55 y) is a spin-1/2 radionuclide used as a gamma-camera and dose-calibrator check source.

isotopes.notes: The preferred barium nucleus. Chemical shift dispersion is small compared with typical linewidths, so spectra are read from the quadrupolar lineshape (CQ up to about 30 MHz in low-symmetry sites) rather than from the isotropic shift.
Lower Q than 137Ba, so narrower central transitions, but lower abundance and gamma; used as a cross-check when 137Ba lineshapes are ambiguous.
Spin-1/2 radionuclide, standard multi-line gamma calibration source (81, 276, 303, 356, 384 keV).

name: Lanthanum
blurb: 139La is 99.91% abundant with spin 7/2 and only a moderate quadrupole moment, making it one of the most receptive quadrupolar nuclei anywhere in the periodic table. In MR chemistry La3+ is the diamagnetic stand-in for the paramagnetic lanthanides, so it defines the zero-shift baseline against which lanthanide-induced shifts and PARACEST offsets are measured.
mrNotes: Xi(139La) = 14.125641 %, reference LaCl3 in D2O; receptivity is about 354 times 13C.
Solid-state isotropic shifts run from -135 ppm in LaF3 to +700 ppm in LaI3, with CQ from 15.6 MHz (LaCl3) to 24.0 MHz (LaI3).
La3+ and Lu3+ are the diamagnetic controls in lanthanide shift reagent and PARACEST series, isolating the hyperfine contribution.
138La (0.090%, 1.03e11 y) is one of very few naturally occurring nuclei with I = 5.

isotopes.notes: Larmor frequency sits just below 2H, so 139La signals can appear in the lock channel region on some spectrometers.

Primordial but radioactive (electron capture and beta-minus, the LaBr3 detector background). Spin 5 gives the largest I(I+1) enhancement in this slice but abundance of 0.09% leaves receptivity at about half that of 13C.

name: Cerium
blurb: Cerium has no NMR-active stable isotope: its four natural nuclides (136, 138, 140, 142) are all even-even with I = 0, so there is nothing to detect. It is paramagnetic (chi_m about +2500e-6 cm3/mol) and redox-active between Ce3+ and Ce4+, which is why ceria nanoparticles appear in MR as relaxation modulators and redox reporters rather than as a spectroscopic nucleus.
mrNotes: Of the elements that have stable isotopes, only cerium and argon have no naturally occurring nuclide with I > 0.
Ce3+ is 4f1 with mu_eff about 2.5 muB, a weak relaxation agent next to Gd3+ (7.9 muB) or Dy3+ (10.6 muB).
Ce4+ is 4f0 and diamagnetic, so the Ce3+/Ce4+ couple gives a genuine paramagnetic on/off switch.

name: Praseodymium
blurb: 141Pr is by a wide margin the most receptive nucleus in the lanthanide block: 100% abundant, I = 5/2, gamma 13.0 MHz/T, with a receptivity of about a third of 1H. Its chemistry is used for shift rather than relaxation, Pr(fod)3 being the upfield-shifting partner to Eu(fod)3 in the original lanthanide shift reagents.
mrNotes: Receptivity relative to 13C is about 1960, the highest of any lanthanide nucleus, though Q = -7.7 fm2 still broadens lines in low-symmetry sites.
Pr3+ is 4f2 with mu_eff about 3.6 muB, so it perturbs chemical shift strongly while adding far less relaxation than Gd3+ or Dy3+.
Pr:YSO and Pr:LaF3 are the standard rare-earth optical quantum memory hosts, read out via 141Pr hyperfine levels.
PrCo5 and Pr-substituted NdFeB are used where coercivity must survive low-temperature or high-demagnetization operation.

isotopes.notes: Quadrupole moment from Stone 2013 (-0.077 b). In Pr3+ compounds the 141Pr line is normally shifted and broadened beyond ordinary solution detection by 4f2 paramagnetism; the high receptivity is realised only in diamagnetic hosts and in NMR of ordered magnets.

name: Neodymium
blurb: Nd2Fe14B is the permanent magnet material behind essentially every low-field and point-of-care MRI system, plus passive shim stacks, MR-conditional motors and Halbach bores. Its own NMR isotopes, 143Nd and 145Nd, are negative-gamma spin-7/2 nuclei with large quadrupole moments and are not practically observable.
mrNotes: Nd2Fe14B reaches remanence near 1.4 T and (BH)max above 400 kJ/m3; Halbach arrays of it give 0.05 to 0.2 T bores with no cryogens and no power supply.
Remanence drifts about -0.12 %/K and the Curie temperature is only 585 K, so Halbach scanners need thermal stabilisation or continuous field tracking.
Dy or Tb substitution at a few weight percent raises coercivity so magnets survive gradient-induced heating and demagnetising fields.
143Nd has gamma = -2.32 MHz/T and Q = -61 fm2; no useful NMR in ordinary samples.

isotopes.notes: Negative gamma. Used in geochemistry as the 147Sm-143Nd decay pair, not in spectroscopy.
Lower gamma and lower abundance than 143Nd; receptivity below that of 13C.

name: Promethium
blurb: Promethium has no stable isotope, no natural abundance and no role in magnetic resonance. 147Pm (2.62 y) is a nearly pure beta emitter with I = 7/2 that shows up in radioluminescent paint and betavoltaic cells, not in imaging.
mrNotes: No susceptibility measurement exists for the metal; Pm2O3 was measured at +2660e-6 cm3/mol, close to the 5I4 free-ion prediction of about +2960e-6.
Pm3+ is 4f4 with mu_eff about 2.7 muB, between Nd3+ and Sm3+, so it would be a poor relaxation agent even if it were available.

isotopes.notes: Beta-minus emitter, Emax 225 keV, essentially no gamma. Receptivity computes to zero because natural abundance is zero.

name: Samarium
blurb: SmCo5 and Sm2Co17 magnets hold their remanence to about -0.03 %/K, roughly four times flatter than NdFeB, and work to 300 C, so they are chosen wherever bore or gradient heating would demagnetise neodymium. 153Sm-EDTMP (Quadramet) is an approved bone-seeking beta therapy for painful skeletal metastases.
mrNotes: Sm3+ is 4f5 with mu_eff only about 1.5 muB, the smallest of the trivalent lanthanides, because L and S nearly cancel; samarium is therefore a poor relaxation agent.
Sm2Co17 has a Curie temperature near 1100 K versus 585 K for Nd2Fe14B, the reason it is used in MR-conditional motors and cryogenic assemblies.
153Sm (46.3 h) emits betas of Emax 810 keV plus a 103 keV gamma (28%) that allows post-therapy SPECT dosimetry.
Both NMR-active samarium isotopes have negative gamma and receptivity well below 13C.

isotopes.notes: Primordial alpha emitter, the parent of the 147Sm-143Nd chronometer. Negative gamma.
Observationally stable (alpha half-life above 2e15 y). Unusually small Q for a deformed rare-earth nucleus, +7.8 fm2.

Magnetic moment is almost exactly zero, mu = -0.00216 nuclear magnetons, giving gamma = -0.011 MHz/T, the smallest of any nucleus in this slice. Quadrupole moment not reliably tabulated. Therapeutic nuclide in Quadramet.

name: Europium
blurb: Eu3+ DOTA-tetraamide complexes are the prototype PARACEST agents: the metal-bound water resonates near +50 ppm from bulk water and exchanges slowly enough (a few thousand per second) to be saturated selectively. Eu2+ is isoelectronic with Gd3+ (4f7, S = 7/2), which makes europium the one lanthanide that can switch between a shift agent and a genuine T1 agent on reduction.
mrNotes: The bound-water CEST peak of EuDOTA-tetraamide chelates sits near +50 ppm, roughly twice the offset of the H4 ring proton, far enough from water for clean selective saturation.
Eu2+ complexes have Gd3+-like S = 7/2 and give real r1 relaxivity, the basis of redox-responsive agents that switch on in hypoxic tissue.
Eu(fod)3 shifts substrate resonances downfield and Pr(fod)3 upfield; these were the original lanthanide shift reagents.
151Eu and 153Eu share I = 5/2 but their quadrupole moments differ by 2.7 times (90.3 versus 241 fm2), a useful internal check on EFG analyses.

isotopes.notes: Slightly more abundant than 151Eu but less than half the gamma and nearly three times the Q, so 151Eu is the practical choice. Also the Mossbauer nucleus of choice for Eu oxidation state.
Higher gamma and smaller Q than 153Eu, receptivity about 11 times higher. Formally an alpha emitter with half-life near 5e18 y, effectively stable.

name: Gadolinium
blurb: Gd3+ is the T1 contrast workhorse because of one specific combination: a half-filled 4f shell giving S = 7/2 and seven unpaired electrons, an orbitally non-degenerate 8S7/2 ground state, and an electronic relaxation time of order 1e-9 s, slow enough that the electron-nucleus dipolar coupling is not motionally averaged before it can relax water protons. Clinical chelates deliver r1 of about 3.5 to 5 mM-1 s-1 at 1.5 T.
mrNotes: Gadolinium metal is ferromagnetic only below its Curie point of 292 K; at 293 K and at body temperature it is paramagnetic, and the Gd3+ ion in every clinical chelate is paramagnetic at all temperatures. The tabulated chi_m of +185000e-6 cm3/mol is quoted at 350 K because 293 K sits essentially at Tc.
The long electronic T1e near 1e-9 s is the discriminator: Dy3+ and Ho3+ have larger moments but T1e near 1e-13 s, which is why they act on T2 and Gd3+ acts on T1.

Macrocyclic DOTA-type chelates have conditional stability log K near 25 and dissociate orders of magnitude more slowly than linear DTPA-type ones, the basis of the NSF and gadolinium-retention risk split.
157Gd has the largest thermal neutron capture cross section of any stable nuclide, about 254000 barns, which underlies gadolinium neutron capture therapy.

isotopes.notes: Tiny negative gamma and a 135 fm2 quadrupole moment; in any Gd3+ compound the line is also destroyed by the ion's own paramagnetism, so gadolinium NMR is never observed in practice.
Even lower gamma than 157Gd. Also a strong neutron absorber (about 61000 barns), contributing with 157Gd to natural Gd's use in reactor control and neutron shielding.

name: Terbium
blurb: 159Tb is 100% abundant with I = 3/2 and a respectable gamma, but Tb3+ paramagnetism (mu_eff 9.7 muB) destroys its own resonance, so terbium reaches MR as a high-moment susceptibility ion and as a radionuclide family. The terbium quadruplet, 149Tb alpha, 152Tb PET, 155Tb SPECT and 161Tb beta, shares one chelate chemistry with the gadolinium imaging agents.
mrNotes: On paper 159Tb receptivity is about 405 times 13C; in Tb3+ compounds the line is unobservable, and terbium NMR is done only in ordered magnets and diamagnetic hosts.
Tb3+ chelates give strong Curie-spin T2 shortening that scales as B0 squared, making them useful as high-field susceptibility markers.
Grain-boundary diffusion of 0.5 to 3 wt% Tb raises NdFeB coercivity with less heavy rare earth than dysprosium.
Terfenol-D (Tb0.3Dy0.7Fe2) is strongly magnetostrictive and must be kept out of the bore; it is also used in some MR-compatible actuator research.

isotopes.notes: The only stable terbium nuclide. Large Q (143.2 fm2) plus 4f8 paramagnetism means the useful measurements are NQR and Mossbauer rather than NMR.

name: Dysprosium
blurb: Dy3+ carries one of the two largest ionic magnetic moments in the periodic table, mu_eff about 10.6 muB, combined with an extremely short electronic relaxation time near 1e-13 s. That pairing makes it a pure T2 and T2* susceptibility agent rather than a T1 agent, and dysprosium chelates were the first bolus-tracking agents for first-pass perfusion imaging.
mrNotes: Dy-DTPA-BMA and Dy-DTPA were used as susceptibility bolus tracers for dynamic perfusion before Gd-based DSC became routine; the effect grows as B0 squared, so it favours 3 T and above.
chi_m is +98000e-6 cm3/mol at 293 K; dysprosium metal is antiferromagnetic below 179 K and ferromagnetic below 85 K, so it is paramagnetic under all MRI conditions.
Dy is the standard heavy-rare-earth dopant that raises NdFeB coercivity and operating temperature in magnet assemblies.
165Dy (2.33 h) ferric hydroxide macroaggregates are used for radiation synovectomy of the knee.

isotopes.notes: Positive gamma, the more receptive of the two. Q of 265 fm2 and 4f9 paramagnetism restrict work to NQR, Mossbauer and ordered-magnet NMR.
Negative gamma. The 25.7 keV transition is a standard Mossbauer line for dysprosium site symmetry.

name: Holmium
blurb: Ho3+ matches Dy3+ for the largest ionic moment at about 10.6 muB, and holmium metal has the highest atomic magnetic moment of any element. Holmium microspheres for liver radioembolization are directly quantifiable by MRI: the holmium payload shows up as R2* and as a susceptibility shift, so the same particles that deliver the dose also report where it went.
mrNotes: 166Ho (26.8 h) combines therapeutic betas with a 81 keV gamma for SPECT and a paramagnetic ion visible on MRI; its ground state is I = 0, so it has no NMR line of its own.
Holmium poly(L-lactic acid) microspheres can be imaged at trace doses before the therapeutic infusion, giving an MRI scout dose rather than a 99mTc-MAA surrogate.
165Ho is 100% abundant with I = 7/2 and gamma 9.06 MHz/T, but 4f10 paramagnetism makes its NMR unobservable in ordinary compounds.
chi_m is +72900e-6 cm3/mol at 293 K; holmium pole pieces have been used to concentrate flux in small-bore high-field magnets at cryogenic temperature.

isotopes.notes: Largest magnetic moment in this slice at +4.16 nuclear magnetons, paired with one of the largest quadrupole moments (+358 fm2). Studied by NQR and by NMR in diamagnetically diluted hosts.

name: Erbium
blurb: Erbium's MR footprint is thin: 167Er is the only NMR-active isotope, with negative gamma and a 357 fm2 quadrupole moment, and Er3+ chelates are weaker T2 agents than dysprosium or holmium. Its clinical use is 169Er colloid for radiosynoviorthesis of finger and toe joints.
mrNotes: Er3+ has mu_eff about 9.6 muB and chi_m +48000e-6 cm3/mol at 293 K, so its relaxation effect is Curie-spin dominated and grows as B0 squared.
167Er is the workhorse nucleus for hyperfine spectroscopy of Er-doped crystals used as telecom-band (1.5 um) quantum memories.
169Er (9.4 d) is a pure low-energy beta emitter, chosen for small joints because its tissue range is under 1 mm.

isotopes.notes: Negative gamma, large Q, and Er3+ paramagnetism; the practical measurements are EPR and optical hyperfine spectroscopy rather than NMR.

name: Thulium
blurb: 169Tm is the only spin-1/2 nucleus in the second half of the lanthanide series, 100% abundant but with a gamma of just 3.52 MHz/T. Thulium's real MR job is done by its chelates: TmDOTP5- is the standard shift reagent that separates intracellular from extracellular 23Na, and TmDOTMA- is the reference paramagnetic thermometry probe.
mrNotes: The TmDOTMA- methyl resonance sits at about -106 ppm and moves roughly 0.6 to 0.7 ppm per degree C, some sixty times the temperature coefficient of water and with opposite sign.
TmDOTP5- shifts the extracellular 23Na resonance clear of the intracellular pool, enabling compartment-resolved 23Na MRS in perfused organs and in vivo.
169Tm receptivity is 5.66e-4 of 1H, about 3.3 times 13C, despite the low gamma, because it is spin-1/2 and 100% abundant.
170Tm (128.6 d) is a compact low-energy photon source investigated for brachytherapy.

isotopes.notes: Spin-1/2 with no quadrupole moment, so linewidths are set by paramagnetism and by chemical shift anisotropy alone. IUPAC defines no reference sample for thulium and no frequency ratio is given here, for the same reason as iridium: Tm3+ is paramagnetic, no diamagnetic thulium reference exists, and a quoted ratio would be an estimate rather than a measurement. mu = -0.2310(15) nuclear magnetons gives gamma = -3.52 MHz/T with an uncertainty of about 0.7 percent, which covers the 3.531 MHz/T of the older tables (mu = 0.2316). The moment is negative, so gamma is negative; tables printing +3.531 are printing its magnitude.

name: Ytterbium
blurb: Yb3+ is 4f13, a single hole, so it gives large hyperfine shifts with short electronic relaxation, which is exactly what a PARACEST agent needs; YbDOTAM-type chelates are used as shift and CEST reporters. 171Yb is spin-1/2 with 14.3% abundance and Xi 17.499306 %, one of the few directly observable heavy-metal nuclei that carries no quadrupolar broadening.
mrNotes: Ytterbium metal is divalent (4f14) and essentially nonmagnetic, chi_m only +67e-6 cm3/mol, in stark contrast to its trivalent neighbours; the paramagnetism of interest belongs to the Yb3+ ion in solution.
171Yb shifts span roughly 0 to +1300 ppm across Yb(II) amides and aryloxides, and homoleptic beta-diketiminates reach about +2650 ppm.
Yb3+ complexes have been used as chemical-shift imaging probes and as temperature-sensitive MRS reporters.
169Yb (32 d) is a low-energy photon brachytherapy source with an average energy near 93 keV.

isotopes.notes: Quadrupolar partner to 171Yb. Q of 280 fm2 makes lines broad in any non-cubic site, so solution work uses 171Yb.
Spin-1/2, receptivity about 4.6 times 13C. Xi is about 0.7% below the value implied by the shielding-corrected moment, the diamagnetic shielding of ytterbium in the reference compound.
